title: Bekhorot 9
description: Rabbi Yehoshua finishes off the sages of Athens, then the mishna on twin and doubtful firstborn donkeys, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and births that coincide exactly, and the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon over benefit from an unredeemed firstborn donkey.
topics: 🌊 The water of the House of the Swallowed: the sages of Athens are defeated
🫏 Twin births, two donkeys, a male and a female: when the priest gets a lamb and when the owner keeps it
🐑 Any lamb redeems: sheep or goat, male or female, old or young, blemished or not
⏱️ Can two births coincide exactly? Rabbi Yirmeya, Abaye and “the males shall be the Lord’s”
🚫 Is an unredeemed firstborn donkey forbidden for benefit? Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Shimon and Ulla’s reasons
💍 Betrothing a woman with second tithe or a firstborn donkey
🐂 “Your ox” and “your flock”: two readings of the verse
🍖 After the neck is broken, and food you can feed to others

a1.he: כִּי מָטֵי לְבֵי בְלִיעֵי, מְלָא כּוּזָא דְּמַיָּא מִבֵּי בְלִיעֵי. כַּד אֲתוֹ, אוֹקְמִינְהוּ קַמֵּי קֵיסָר. חֲזָנְהוּ דַּהֲווֹ מְעַנִּי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי לָאו נִינְהוּ. שְׁקַל מֵעַפְרַיְיהוּ וּשְׁדָא עִילָּוַיְיהוּ, אַקְשׁוֹ לְאַפֵּי מַלְכָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל דְּבָעֵית עֲבֵיד בְּהוּ.

a2.he: אַיְיתִינְהוּ מַיָּא דְּאַיְיתִי מִבֵּי בְלִיעֵי, שְׁדִינְהוּ בְּתִיגְדָּא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַלְיוּהּ לְהוּ וְאֵיזִילוּ לְכוּ. מְלוֹ וּשְׁדוֹ בֵּיהּ קַמָּאֵי קַמָּאֵי, וּבְלַע לְהוּ, מְלוֹ עַד דְּשָׁמֵיט כַּתְפַּיְיהוּ, וּבְלוֹ לְהוּ וַאֲזוּל.

a3.he: מַתְנִי׳ חֲמוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן טָלֶה אֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן, זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — מַפְרִישׁ טָלֶה אֶחָד לְעַצְמוֹ.

a4.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲמוֹרָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן שְׁנֵי טְלָאִים לַכֹּהֵן. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה — נוֹתֵן טָלֶה אֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן. שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת — אֵין לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

a5.he: אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה, וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה, וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן טָלֶה אֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן; זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — מַפְרִישׁ טָלֶה אֶחָד לְעַצְמוֹ.

a6.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה״, מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים, זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, גָּדוֹל וְקָטָן, תָּמִים וּבַעַל מוּם, פּוֹדֶה בּוֹ פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה, נִכְנָס לְדִיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר, וְאִם מֵת — נֶהֱנִין בּוֹ.

a7.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי — הָאָמַר אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם!

a8.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דִּכְתִיב ״הַזְּכָרִים לַה׳״.

a10.he: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי — הָאָמַר אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דִּכְתִיב ״הַזְּכָרִים לַה׳״.

a11.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, דְּלָא מוֹקֵי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי — הַיְינוּ דְּלָא קָתָנֵי ״וְיָצְאוּ שְׁנֵי רָאשֵׁיהֶן כְּאֶחָד״, אֶלָּא לְאַבָּיֵי — לִיתְנֵי ״וְיָצְאוּ שְׁנֵי רָאשֵׁיהֶן כְּאֶחָד״!

a12.he: וְעוֹד, תַּנְיָא: חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים, וְיָצְאוּ שְׁנֵי רָאשֵׁיהֶן כְּאֶחָד, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶן לַכֹּהֵן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַזְּכָרִים לַה׳״.

a13.he: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב הַאי, בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף הוּא דִּכְתִיב! אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַזְּכָרִים לַה׳״, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְאַבָּיֵי, תְּיוּבְתָּא.

b1.he: וְרַבָּנַן, לֵימָא קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן מִקְצָת רֶחֶם מַקְדֵּישׁ? דְּאִי כּוּלֵּיהּ רֶחֶם מַקְדֵּישׁ — נְהִי דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, חֲצִיצָה מִיהָא אִיכָּא!

b2.he: אָמַר רַב: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ.

b3.he: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — מַפְרִישׁ טָלֶה כּוּ׳. וְכֵיוָן דִּלְעַצְמוֹ הוּא, לְמָה לִי לְאַפְרוֹשֵׁי? לְאַפְקוֹעֵי לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ.

b4.he: אַלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מַפְקַע לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ, אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.

b5.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ פְּדִיָּיה וּמוּתָּר? וְלָא?! וַהֲרֵי בְּכוֹר אָדָם שֶׁצָּרִיךְ פְּדִיָּיה וּמוּתָּר! אֶלָּא, יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּשֶׂה וּמוּתָּר?

b6.he: וּמִי הִקְפִּידָה?! וְהָא רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ בְּשִׁילְקֵי בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ! בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ לָא קָאָמְרִינַן, כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן שֶׁלֹּא בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה לְאַפְקוֹעֵי לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ בְּשֶׂה?

b7.he: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּכֶסֶף צוֹרִי, וּתְנַן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּמֵזִיד — קִידֵּשׁ!

b8.he: בְּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר נָמֵי מִיקַּדְּשָׁא, כִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אִשָּׁה יוֹדַעַת שֶׁאֵין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי מִתְחַלֵּל עַל יָדָהּ, וְעוֹלָה וְאוֹכַלְתּוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.

b9.he: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִשָּׁה יוֹדַעַת דְּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר אִיסּוּרָא אִית בֵּיהּ, וּפָרְקָא לֵיהּ בְּשֶׂה, וּמַקְדְּשָׁא בְּהָךְ דְּבֵינֵי וּבֵינֵי.

b10.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי טַעְמֵאּ? אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁפִּדְיוֹנוֹ מוּתָּר וְהוּא אָסוּר?

b11.he: וְלָא? וַהֲרֵי שְׁבִיעִית, דְּפִדְיוֹנָהּ מוּתָּר, וְהִיא אֲסוּרָה!

b12.he: שְׁבִיעִית נָמֵי פִּדְיוֹנָהּ אָסוּר, דְּאָמַר מָר: הָאַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן אָסוּר.

b13.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּהַאי קְרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּתַנְיָא: ״לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ״ — אֲבָל אַתָּה עוֹבֵד בְּשֶׁלְּךָ וּבְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים, ״וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ״ — אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז שֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

b14.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ״ — אֲבָל אַתָּה עוֹבֵד בִּבְכוֹר אָדָם, ״לֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ״ — אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז בְּכוֹר חֲמוֹר.

b15.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמַעוֹטֵי שֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים לְמָה לִי? וְתוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בְּכוֹר אָדָם נָמֵי נֵימָא דַּאֲסִיר!

b16.he: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא ״שׁוֹרֶךָ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי בְּכוֹר אָדָם הוּא דַּאֲתָא, כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּ״צֹאנֶךָ״. דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹי חַיֶּיבֶת בִּבְכוֹרָה, וְכִי אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְמִישְׁרֵי בְּגִזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה.

b17.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹי פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, וּלְעִנְיַן גִּזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא, כִּי אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר.

b18.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״צֹאנֶךָ״ וְ״שׁוֹרֶךָ״, אַטּוּ ״צֹאנֶךָ״. אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, ״שׁוֹרֶךָ״ וְ״צֹאנֶךָ״ לְמָה לִי? קַשְׁיָא.

b19.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְאַחַר עֲרִיפָה, שֶׁהוּא אָסוּר.

b21.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ דְּתַנְיָא: הָעׇרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, וְשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, וְצִיפּוֹרֵי מְצוֹרָע, וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר, וּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב — כּוּלָּן מִטַּמְּאִין טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין.

b22.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין, וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב שֶׁמְּטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין, הוֹאִיל וְהָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.

b23.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? דִּכְתִיב: ״מִכׇּל הָאֹכֶל אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל״, אוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים — קָרוּי אוֹכֶל, שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים — אֵינוֹ קָרוּי אוֹכֶל.

messages.text: 9a
Continued from 8b: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya has defeated the sages of Athens in debate and is sailing them to the emperor; on the way he took out some of the dirt of Athens.

When they reached the House of the Swallowed, a location in the sea where the water absorbs everything in its vicinity, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya filled up a small jug of water from the House of the Swallowed. When they arrived, he presented the sages of Athens before the emperor. The emperor saw that the sages of Athens were suffering due to their having been taken captive.

notes.he: מים שבאוקיינוס שבולעים כל מימות שבעולם שנופלין בו ומביאין אותם עד תהום ופולטות אותן והיינו דכתיב (קהלת א׳:ז׳) והים איננו מלא:
notes.en: To Bei Bli’ei: waters in the ocean that swallow all the waters of the world that fall into it, carry them down to the deep and spit them out. This is what is written: “And the sea is not full” (Ecclesiastes 1:7).

notes.he: פ"ה מי אוקיינוס שבולעות כל מימות שבעולם ופולטות אותן דרך תהום דכתיב והים איננו מלא וקשה דבסמוך קאמר שדינהו בתיגרא שם כלי ושוב היאך יורדין לתהום ואי מפרש גומא או חריץ ניחא ויתכן מי בליעי שם מקום מדאמר שם בי בליעי אית ביה תלתא צלמי חד מטי ידי' ארישיה חד אליביה בתרא דכולהו מחוי בידיה לאחוריה:
notes.en: Bei Bli’ei: Rashi explained: the waters of the ocean, which swallow all the waters of the world and spit them out by way of the deep, as it is written: “And the sea is not full.” But this is difficult, since just afterward it says that he poured it into a tigra, which is the name of a utensil; how, then, would they go down into the deep? If one explains [tigra as] a pit or a trench, it works out. And it may be that Bei Bli’ei is the name of a place, since it is said there [elsewhere]: “In Bei Bli’ei there are three statues: one with its hand on its head, one on its heart, and the last of them points with its hand behind it.”

notes.he: מקום שיש בים שבולעין מים אחרים ואיכא דאמרי היינו בארה של מרים:
notes.en: When he reached Bei Bli’ei: a place in the sea that swallows other waters. And some say this is the well of Miriam.

notes.he: מעונים ושפלים לפי שלא היו בארצם:
notes.en: Me’anei: afflicted and downcast, because they were not in their own land.

notes.he: כמי שגלה ממקומו ולא היה להם מענה לשון:
notes.en: That they were me’anei: like one exiled from his place, and they had no answer on their tongue.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehoshua These individuals cannot be the sages of Athens, because those sages are strong and arrogant.

Rabbi Yehoshua took some of the dirt that he had taken from Athens and threw it upon them. When they smelled the scent of their own soil they began to act like themselves again, and they spoke with arrogance before the king.

notes.he: העיזו ודברו קשות את המלך כשהריחו ריח ארצם סבורים להיות קרובים לארצם:
notes.en: Ikshu: they grew bold and spoke harshly to the king. When they smelled the scent of their land, they thought they were near their land.

notes.he: כשהרגישו עפרם גבה לבן על עפרתן ואקשו לאפי מלכא והיו משיבין דברים לפני המלך בגאוה:
notes.en: They spoke harshly before the king: when they sensed their soil, their hearts grew proud over their soil, and they spoke harshly before the king, answering him arrogantly.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehoshua You may do with them whatever you wish.

notes.he: לר' יהושע כל דבעית עביד בהו:
notes.en: He said: to Rabbi Yehoshua: Do with them whatever you wish.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua brought the water that he had brought from the House of the Swallowed and poured it into a utensil [betigada].

notes.he: בכלי. ל"א בתינארא חבית:
notes.en: Betigda: in a utensil. Another version: betinara, a barrel.

notes.he: בכלי בכד גדול:
notes.en: He poured it into a tigra: into a utensil, a large jug.

messages.text: Fill it up and go on your way.

They filled and poured one by one, i.e., they filled the utensil by pouring in water numerous times, and each time the utensil swallowed up the water. They continued to fill it until their shoulders became disjointed. In this manner, the sages of Athens were defeated.

notes.he: נשמטו שכמם:
notes.en: Until their shoulders became disjointed: their shoulders slipped out of place.

notes.he: בלו והלכו לאבדון:
notes.en: And they wore away and went: they wasted away and went to destruction.

notes.he: מינייהו וכלו ואזיל:
notes.en: Until their shoulders slipped: out of place, and they wasted away and went.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of a female donkey that had not previously given birth and now gave birth to two male offspring, as there is no doubt that one of them is firstborn, its owner gives one lamb to the priest in redemption of that firstborn.

notes.he: בפדיון דממה נפשך חד מינייהו בכור שפטר את הרחם:
notes.en: Mishna. He gives one lamb to the priest: as redemption, since either way one of them is a firstborn that opened the womb.

notes.he: שמעולם לא ילדה אלא עכשיו וילדה ב' זכרים:
notes.en: His donkey that had not given birth: that had never given birth until now, and it bore two males.

notes.he: בשביל פדיון אותו שיצא תחלה:
notes.en: He gives one lamb to the priest: as redemption for the one that came out first.

messages.text: If it gave birth to a male and a female and it is not known which was born first, he designates one lamb as firstborn in case the male was born first. Nevertheless, since it is merely a monetary debt to the priest, the burden of proof rests upon the claimant, in this case the priest. Due to that uncertainty, the priest can offer no proof and the owner keeps the lamb for himself.

notes.he: ואין ידוע אם זכר תחלה והרי הוא בכור או נקבה יצאתה תחלה ואין כאן בכור:
notes.en: A male and a female: and it is not known whether the male came out first, in which case it is a firstborn, or the female came out first, and there is no firstborn here.

notes.he: משום ספק ומפקיע עליו קדושת פטר חמור:
notes.en: He designates a lamb: because of the uncertainty, and thereby removes from it [the donkey] the sanctity of a firstborn donkey.

notes.he: שהוא בעצמו יאכל הטלה ולא יתננו לכהן דכהן הוי מוציא מחבירו ועליו הראייה להביא עדים שהזכר יצא תחלה ואיסורא ליכא דאפי' פטר חמור גמור שפדאו בשה אין קדושה לא בו ולא בפדיונו כדקתני במתניתין ואם מת נהנה בו אלא גזל הוא דאיכא אם אינו נותן את הטלה לכהן דממונא הוא והכא ליכא גזל דספק הוא:
notes.en: And it is for himself: he himself eats the lamb and does not give it to the priest, since the priest would be extracting from his fellow, and the burden is on him to bring witnesses that the male came out first. And there is no prohibition involved, since even with a definite firstborn donkey redeemed with a lamb there is sanctity neither in it nor in its redemption, as the mishna teaches: “And if it dies, one may derive benefit from it.” There is only [a question of] theft if he does not give the lamb to the priest, since it is a monetary matter; and here there is no theft, since it is uncertain.

notes.he: וא"ת לר' יוסי הגלילי דאמר אפשר לצמצם אם יצאו שניהם בבת אחת אין הזכר קדוש לפי מה שפי' לעיל נקבה חוצצת ועוד תנן לקמן בפ' שני (בכורות דף יז:) זכר ונקבה אין לכהן כלום משמע דקאי איצאו ב' ראשיהן כאחת דרישא שהנקבה מבטלת בכורת זכר שגם היא פטרה בכורת רחם וא"כ סמוך מיעוט דבבת אחת למחצה דנקבות קודמות והוו להו זכרים קודמים מיעוטא וי"ל כדפריך לעיל בספק מועט החמירו להפריש טלה לעצמו:
notes.en: A male and a female, he designates a lamb for himself: And if you say: according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says it is possible for births to coincide exactly, if both came out at once the male is not consecrated, according to what was explained above, that the female interposes. Furthermore, we learn below in the second chapter (Bekhorot 17b): “A male and a female, the priest has nothing,” which seems to refer to “their two heads came out as one” in the first clause: the female cancels the male’s firstborn status, since she too opened the womb. If so, join the slight chance of their coming out at once to the even chance that the female came first, and the male’s coming first is the lesser chance. [Why, then, designate a lamb?] One may answer, as [the Gemara] argued above: in the case of a slight uncertainty they were stringent, [requiring him] to designate a lamb for himself.

notes.he: ואם ילדה זכר ונקבה ואינו יודע איזה יצא ראשון אי הזכר שהוא קדוש בבכורה מפריש טלה אחד כדי להפקיע קדושת בכור ספק להפקיע איסורו:
notes.en: And if it bore a male and a female and he does not know which came out first, [and perhaps it was] the male, which is sacred with firstborn sanctity, he designates one lamb to abrogate the sanctity of the uncertain firstborn, to abrogate its forbidden status.

notes.he: אותו טלה יהיה לעצמו של ישראל ויהיה חולין גמור ומותר לאוכלו מ"ט משום דאמרינן המוציא מחברו עליו הראיה וכיון שהכהן אינו יכול להביא ראיה שהזכר יצא ראשון הלכך הוא לעצמו של ישראל:
notes.en: And it: that lamb belongs to the Israelite himself, is fully non-sacred, and may be eaten. What is the reason? Because we say: the burden of proof rests on the one who extracts from his fellow; and since the priest cannot bring proof that the male came out first, it belongs to the Israelite himself.

messages.text: If an individual has two donkeys, and both of his two donkeys had not previously given birth and they now gave birth to two males, one each, the owner gives two lambs to the priest.

notes.dh: שתי חמוריו שלא בכרו וילדו שני זכרים נותן שני טלאים לכהן
notes.he: הכא ניחא דאצטריך לאשמועינן אין פודה וחוזר ופודה כל זמן שלא ניתן ליד כהן כדפריך לעיל בפירקא (בכורות דף ד:) אבל לקמן פ"ב דקתני כי האי גוונא גבי בכורות בהמה טהורה ליכא למימר הכי י"ל קמ"ל לא תלינן להעמיד הממון בחזקת בעלים שהאחת טנפה ונמוח הוולד ואחת ילדה שני זכרים ומיהו לקמן פרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מח:) קתני כה"ג גבי נשים ליכא למימר הכי שכל אחת יודעת בעצמה מה שילדה וי"ל אגב דתנייה הכא תנייה התם א"נ ניחא ליה לפרש כל גווני ואע"ג דלא צריכי כדקתני זכר ונקבה נותן אחד לכהן דלא צריכא כלל:
notes.en: His two donkeys had not given birth and they bore two males, he gives two lambs to the priest: Here it works out, since this was needed to teach us that one does not redeem [with one lamb] and then redeem again [with the same lamb] so long as it has not been given into the priest’s hand, as was argued above in this chapter (Bekhorot 4b). But below, in the second chapter, where the same case is taught with firstborns of kosher animals, one cannot say this. One may answer: it teaches us that we do not suppose, so as to leave the money with its owner, that one of them miscarried a shapeless mass whose fetus dissolved and the other bore two males. However, below, in the chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 48b), the same case is taught with women, and one cannot say this, since each woman knows for herself what she bore. One may answer: since it taught it here, it taught it there. Alternatively, it prefers to spell out every case even where they are not needed, as it teaches “a male and a female, he gives one to the priest,” which is not needed at all.

messages.text: If they together gave birth to a male and a female or to two males and a female, he gives one lamb to the priest, as one of the males is certainly a firstborn.

notes.dh: שני חמורים כו' זכר ונקבה נותן טלה לכהן
notes.he: בשביל הזכר:
notes.en: Two donkeys … a male and a female, he gives a lamb to the priest: for the male.

notes.he: דחדא ילדה זכר וחדא ילדה זכר ונקבה:
notes.en: Or two males and a female: one bore a male, and the other bore a male and a female.

notes.he: דהא איכא חד זכר ודאי בכור ואידך דהוי ספק דשמא הנקבה יצאתה תחלה מפריש טלה והוא לעצמו:
notes.en: He gives one lamb to the priest: since there is one male that is certainly a firstborn. For the other, which is uncertain, since perhaps the female came out first, he designates a lamb and it is his own.

notes.dh: שני זכרים ונקבה נותן טלה אחד לכהן
notes.he: לכאורה מפריש טלה אחד מספק לעצמו וכן מוכח לקמן פרק שני (בכורות דף יח:) דגבי שני זכרים ונקבה אחד לו ואחד לכהן (דמוכח) משום דקדושת בכור חלה על שתיהם וכן פי' בקונטרס מפריש עוד טלה והוא לעצמו:
notes.en: Two males and a female, he gives one lamb to the priest: Apparently he also designates one lamb for himself because of the uncertainty. So it is evident below in the second chapter (Bekhorot 18b), where for two males and a female, one is his and one is the priest’s, because the sanctity of a firstborn takes effect on both of them. And so Rashi explained: he designates another lamb and it is his own.

notes.he: שאחת ילדה זכר ואחת ילדה נקבה נותן טלה אחד לכהן. בשביל אותו שילדה זכר:
notes.en: A male and a female: one bore a male and one bore a female; he gives one lamb to the priest, for the one that bore the male.

messages.text: If they together gave birth to two females and a male or to two males and two females, the priest receives nothing, as perhaps the two firstborn were females.

notes.he: ספק הן דשמא כל חד וחד ילדה זכר ונקבה ושמא נקבות יצאו תחלה הילכך אין כאן לכהן כלום אלא מפריש עליהן שני טלאים לאפקועי איסוריהן והן לעצמו:
notes.en: Two males and two females: these are uncertain, since perhaps each one bore a male and a female, and perhaps the females came out first. Therefore the priest has nothing here; rather, he designates two lambs for them to abrogate their forbidden status, and they are his own.

notes.he: שכל אחד ילדה זכר ונקבה ואינו יודע איזה יצא ראשון:
notes.en: Two males and two females: each one bore a male and a female, and he does not know which came out first.

notes.he: אבל יפריש ב' טלאים לעצמו:
notes.en: The priest has nothing here: but he designates two lambs for himself.

messages.text: If one of his donkeys had previously given birth and one had not previously given birth and they now together gave birth to two males, the owner gives one lamb to the priest as redemption for the firstborn male.

notes.he: אחת שבכרה כבר ואחת שלא בכרה מעולם אלא עכשיו וילדו ב' זכרים כו':
notes.en: One had already given birth and one had never given birth until now, and they bore two males etc.

messages.text: If they together gave birth to a male and a female he designates one lamb for himself, as it is uncertain whether or not the male was a firstborn and the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

notes.dh: אחת ביכרה וכו' זכר ונקבה מפריש טלה והוא לעצמו
notes.he: דשמא אותה שלא ביכרה ילדה את הנקבה:
notes.en: One had given birth etc., a male and a female, he designates a lamb and it is his own: since perhaps the one that had not given birth bore the female.

messages.caption: The mishna’s cases: what goes to the priest, and what the owner designates and keeps. Rashi and Tosafot fill in two cells; one is marked “implied.”

messages.text: From where is it derived that the firstborn of a donkey is redeemed with a lamb? It is derived from a verse, as it is stated: “And you shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb [seh]” (Exodus 34:20).

verse.he: וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם־לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ כֹּל בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה וְלֹא־יֵרָאוּ פָנַי רֵיקָם׃
verse.en:
But the firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you must redeem every male first-born among your children.
None shall appear before Me empty-handed.

notes.he: ארישא קאי כלומר מנא לן דפדיון פטר חמור בשה שנאמר ופטר חמור תפדה בשה:
notes.en: As it is stated: “And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb”: this refers back to the first clause. That is to say: from where do we derive that a firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb? As it is stated: “And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb.”

messages.text: The owner may give a lamb either from sheep or from goats; from males or females, from older or younger animals, and from unblemished or blemished animals.

notes.he: בין שה זכר בין נקבה:
notes.en: Male or female: whether the lamb is male or female.

notes.he: האי שנאמר לא משמע עלה דמלתא דקאמר אלא בבא לחודה קאמר כלומר האי דכתיב ופטר חמור תפדה בשה לא שנא בשה לחוד אלא אפי' בעז או בזכר או בנקבה או בגדול או בקטן או בתם או בבעל מום כשר לפדות:
notes.en: As it is stated: “And the firstborn of a donkey…”: this “as it is stated” does not refer to the matter just said; it is a clause of its own. That is, what is written, “And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a seh,” does not mean only with a sheep: even with a goat, a male or a female, a large or a small one, an unblemished or a blemished one, it is fit to redeem with.

messages.text: If the priest returns the lamb to the owner, he may redeem firstborn donkeys with it many times.

notes.he: שאם חזר כהן ונתנו לו לישראל ויש לו פטרי חמורים יכול לפדותן בו:
notes.en: And he may redeem with it many times: if the priest gave it back to the Israelite, and he has [other] firstborn donkeys, he can redeem them with it.

notes.he: ופודה בו פעמים הרבה כלומר אם בא לידו אותו שה שנתנו לכהן בפדיון פטר חמור אחד וחזר הכהן ומכרו לו או נתנו לו יכול לפדות בו באותו שה פטר חמור אחר בכל עת שיבא לידו יכול לחזור ולפדות בו או שאם היה כן שהפרישו לעצמו כדאמרן ונולד לו פטר חמור אחר ודאי יכול לפדותו באותו שה עצמו ואותו טלה שהפרישו לעצמו הוי חולין גמורין ונכנס לדיר להתעשר עם שאר כבשיו:
notes.en: And he may redeem with it many times: that is, if the lamb he gave the priest to redeem one firstborn donkey came back into his hand, because the priest sold it to him or gave it to him, he can redeem another firstborn donkey with that same lamb; whenever it comes into his hand he can redeem with it again. Or, if he designated it for himself as we said, and another firstborn donkey was born to him, he can certainly redeem it with that same lamb. And the lamb he designated for himself is fully non-sacred and enters the pen to be tithed with the rest of his sheep.

messages.text: In a case where he designates a lamb due to uncertainty and keeps it for himself, it is his in every sense. Consequently, it enters the pen in order to be tithed with the other non-sacred animals (see Leviticus 27:32), and if it dies, one may derive benefit from its carcass.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: It enters etc.: this is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: ואם מת נהנה בו ישראל שהפריש שה ליתנו לכהן בשביל פטר חמור ודאי ולא הספיק ליתנו לכהן עד שמת נהנה בו כהן בעורו ובנבילתו דמעידנא דאפרשיה זכה בו כהן וברשותיה קאי:
notes.en: And if it dies, one may derive benefit from it: an Israelite who designated a lamb to give to the priest for a definite firstborn donkey, and it died before he managed to give it to the priest: the priest may benefit from its hide and its carcass, since from the moment he designated it the priest acquired it, and it stands in his possession.

messages.text: Gemara
Who is the tanna who taught that if a female donkey that had never given birth before gives birth to twin males, the owner gives only one lamb to the priest?
messages.quote: a female donkey that had not previously given birth and now gave birth to two male offspring

notes.he: דחמורה שלא ביכרה וילדה שני זכרים דאינו נותן לכהן אלא חד טלה:
notes.en: Gemara. Who taught it: [the ruling about] a donkey that had not given birth and bore two males, that he gives the priest only one lamb.

notes.dh: מאן תנא א"ר ירמיה דלא כר' יוסי הגלילי
notes.he: פ"ה מאן תנא דאמרינן שילדה שני זכרים אינו נותן אלא חד טלה לכהן וקשה לפי' דהכא אפי' ר"י הגלילי מודה מדלא קתני במתניתין ויצאו שני ראשיהן כאחד כדקתני בפרק שני (לקמן בכורות יז.) וכיון דלא ראינו שיצאו בבת אחת מספק לא אמרי' בבת אחת יצאו אפי' לר"י הגלילי דלא שכיחא וצריך לפרש דנהי דמספק מודה ר' יוסי הגלילי דאין נותן לכהן אלא חד טלה מ"מ בספק מועט טוב להחמיר בדבר ולהפריש טלה שני לעצמו:
notes.en: Who taught it? Rabbi Yirmeya says: Not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: Rashi explained: who taught that [if a donkey] bore two males, he gives only one lamb to the priest? But this is difficult for his explanation, since here even Rabbi Yosei HaGelili agrees, as the mishna does not teach “and their two heads came out as one,” as it does in the second chapter (Bekhorot 17a); and since we did not see that they came out at once, we do not say out of uncertainty that they came out at once, even according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, since it is uncommon. One must explain: granted that in a case of uncertainty Rabbi Yosei HaGelili agrees that he gives the priest only one lamb, nevertheless, with a slight uncertainty it is good to be stringent and to designate a second lamb for himself.

messages.text: It is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. As if it were in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, doesn’t he say in a later mishna (17a) with regard to a kosher animal that gave birth to two males and both their heads emerged as one, that it is possible that both births coincided precisely, and therefore both of the twins are given to the priest? According to his opinion, in the case here as well, two lambs should be given to the priest. The mishna clearly follows the opinion of the Rabbis that only one of the two is considered a firstborn.

notes.he: דאמרינן לקמן בפ' הלוקח עובר פרתו (בכורות דף יז.) רחל שלא ביכרה וילדה שני זכרים ר' יוסי הגלילי אומר שניהם לכהן דאפשר לצמצם ששניהן יצאו כאחד ושניהן בכורות:
notes.en: Not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: as we say below, in the chapter HaLokeaḥ Ubar Parato (Bekhorot 17a): a ewe that had not given birth and bore two males, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says both go to the priest, since it is possible for the births to coincide exactly, so that both came out as one and both are firstborns.

notes.he: הא אמר באידך פירקין דאפשר לצמצם כדאמרי' ריה"ג אומר שניהם לכהן שנאמר הזכרים לה' הכא נמי אי ר' יוסי הוא נותן ב' טלאים לכהן מיבעי ליה דהא אית ליה אפשר לצמצם דיצאו שניהם כאחת:
notes.en: As if it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: he says in the other chapter that it is possible for births to coincide exactly, as we say: “Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says both go to the priest, as it is stated: ‘The males shall be the Lord’s.’” Here too, if it is Rabbi Yosei, he should have to give two lambs to the priest, since he holds it is possible for births to coincide exactly, so that both came out as one.

messages.text: You may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and it is different there with regard to a kosher animal, as it is written: “Every firstborn that you have of animals, the males shall be the Lord’s” (Exodus 13:12), i.e., the word “males” is written in the plural. This indicates that if they emerged simultaneously they both have firstborn status. By contrast, with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey, only one has firstborn status.
messages.quote: It is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

notes.he: גבי רחל:
notes.en: It is different there, as it is written: with a ewe.

notes.he: דמשמע שנים אבל בפטר חמור דלא כתיב ביה הזכרים א"נ אפשר לצמצם לא קדשי:
notes.en: The males shall be the Lord’s: which implies two. But with a firstborn donkey, where “the males” is not written, even if it is possible for the births to coincide exactly, they are not consecrated.

notes.he: גבי בכור בהמה טהורה הזכרים לה' משמע שניהם אבל הכא בפדיון פטר חמור לא כתיב הזכרים:
notes.en: It is different there: with a firstborn kosher animal, “the males shall be the Lord’s” implies both of them; but here, with the redemption of a firstborn donkey, “the males” is not written.

messages.text: But let him derive from the halakha of a firstborn kosher animal that the halakha of a firstborn donkey is the same.
messages.quote: the males shall be the Lord’s

notes.he: בכור בהמה טמאה מבהמה טהורה:
notes.en: But let him derive from it: the firstborn of a non-kosher animal from a kosher animal.

messages.text: The Merciful One restricted this principle to the case of a firstborn kosher animal, where it is written: “The males shall be the Lord’s.” The word “the” indicates that two males can be considered firstborn only in the case of a firstborn kosher animal.

notes.he: הזכרים ה"א יתירה משמע זו ולא אחרת:
notes.en: But the Merciful One restricted: “the males”; the extra letter heh [“the”] implies this one and not another.

notes.he: דכתיב הזכרים אחרינא דמייתר כל פטר רחם הזכרים למעט אחריני דהני דקדושת הגוף נינהו הזכרים לה' תרוייהו אבל בקדושת דמים לא:
notes.en: But the Merciful One restricted “the males”: since it is written “the males,” which is superfluous after “all that opens the womb,” “the males” excludes the others: for these, which have inherent sanctity, “the males shall be the Lord’s,” both of them; but not with sanctity of value.

messages.text: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as if it follows the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, doesn’t he say it is possible that both births coincide precisely, and if they were born simultaneously both are considered firstborn?
messages.lead: Some say there is another version of this discussion:

messages.text: You may even say it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and it is different there, as it is written: “The males shall be the Lord’s.”

Granted, according to Rabbi Yirmeya, who does not interpret the mishna in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, that is the reason that it does not teach: And both of their heads emerged as one, as stated in the mishna where the ruling of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is taught; according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, this is impossible.
messages.quote: You may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili

notes.dh: בשלמא לר' ירמיה דלא מוקי לה כרבי יוסי
notes.he: דקמפרש טעמא דמתניתין משום (טעמא) דאי אפשר לצמצם שלא יצא ראש האחד תחלה דהוי פטר רחם היינו דלא קתני במתני' יצאו שני ראשיהן כאחד כי היכי דתני לקמן בפירקין (בכורות דף יז.) גבי מילתיה דרבי יוסי הגלילי דהא לא אפשר:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Yirmeya, who does not establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei: since he explains the reason of the mishna as being that it is impossible for the births to coincide exactly, so that the head of one did not come out first and open the womb. That is why the mishna does not teach “their two heads came out as one,” as it teaches below (Bekhorot 17a) in connection with the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: since it is not possible.

notes.he: דפסיק ואמר דלא כר' יוסי היינו דלא קתני הכא בחמור שלא בכרה ויצאו ראשיהם כאחד כדתני במתניתין דאידך פירקא דאיירי בה ר' יוסי אלמא דהא מתני' לאו ר' יוסי היא:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Yirmeya: who states flatly that it is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, that is why it does not teach here, with a donkey that had not given birth, “and their heads came out as one,” as it teaches in the mishna of the other chapter, where Rabbi Yosei takes part. Evidently this mishna is not Rabbi Yosei’s.

messages.text: But according to Abaye, who holds that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and such an occurrence is possible, let the mishna teach: And both of their heads emerged as one, indicating that in this case even Rabbi Yosei HaGelili agrees only one lamb is given to the priest.

notes.he: דאפשר לצמצם וטעמא משום מיעוט דהזכרים ליתני ויצאו ראשיהן כאחת דשמעינן מינה רבותא:
notes.en: But according to Abaye: [who holds] it is possible for the births to coincide exactly, and the reason [only one lamb is given] is the restriction of “the males,” let it teach “and their heads came out as one,” and we would learn a novelty from it.

notes.he: דבעי לאוקמה כר' יוסי ליתני הכא ויצאו ב' ראשים כאחד ואע"ג דמצומצמין אינהו דאפשר לצמצם חד הוא דקדוש דהא מיעט רחמנא הזכרים. ועוד הא אשכחן בברייתא דתני ויצאו ב' ראשים כאחד ריה"ג אמר שניהם לכהן שנאמר הזכרים לה':
notes.en: But according to Abaye: who wants to establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, let it teach here “and two heads came out as one”: even though they coincided exactly, since it is possible for births to coincide exactly, only one is consecrated, since the Merciful One restricted “the males.” And furthermore, we find a baraita that teaches: “and two heads came out as one, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: Both go to the priest, as it is stated: ‘The males shall be the Lord’s.’”

messages.text: Furthermore, it is taught in a baraita:
Both of them are given to the priest, as it is stated: “The males shall be the Lord’s.”
messages.lead: If one’s donkey had not previously given birth and now gave birth to two males, and both of their heads emerged as one,

notes.he: בהדיא דאפי' בבהמה טמאה אמר נמי רבי יוסי שניהן לכהן:
notes.en: And furthermore, it is taught: explicitly, that even with a non-kosher animal Rabbi Yosei says both go to the priest.

messages.text: But when this verse is written, isn’t it written with regard to a firstborn kosher animal, which has inherent sanctity, unlike a firstborn donkey?
messages.quote: as it is stated: “The males shall be the Lord’s.”

notes.he: בבהמה טהורה:
notes.en: Inherent sanctity: a kosher animal.

messages.text: Rather, because it is stated with regard to a kosher animal: “The males shall be the Lord’s,” this serves as the basis for the halakha with regard to the firstborn of a non-kosher animal that both males can be considered firstborn.

notes.he: בבכור בהמה טהורה דשמעינן מינה דאפשר לצמצם אמר ה"ה לפטר חמור:
notes.en: Rather, because it is stated “the males”: with the firstborn of a kosher animal, from which we learn that it is possible for births to coincide exactly, he said the same holds for a firstborn donkey.

messages.text: If so, the refutation of the opinion of Abaye is in fact a conclusive refutation, and the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, not that of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
messages.quote: You may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili

notes.he: והא כי כתיב האי הזכרים לה' בקדושת הגוף כתיב והיכי מצי למילף לפטר חמור מיניה אלא משום שנאמר הזכרים לה' גבי בכור בהמה טהורה ילפינן נמי מיניה לפטר חמור ואם איתא דמתני' ר' יוסי היא ליתני נמי במתני' ויצאו אלא מדלא קתני ש"מ דלא ר' יוסי היא אלא רבנן ותיובתא לאביי:
notes.en: But when this “the males shall be the Lord’s” is written, it is written about inherent sanctity; how can he derive a firstborn donkey from it? Rather, because “the males shall be the Lord’s” is stated with a firstborn kosher animal, we derive a firstborn donkey from it as well. And if the mishna were Rabbi Yosei’s, let the mishna also teach “and they came out [as one].” Rather, since it does not teach it, learn from this that it is not Rabbi Yosei but the Rabbis, and this is a refutation of Abaye.

messages.text: 9b

And with regard to the opinion of the Rabbis, let us say the Rabbis hold that even a portion of the mouth of the womb sanctifies a firstborn despite the offspring never having touched the entire area.

notes.he: הנוגע בבכור מקדשו דנהי דאי אפשר לצמצם וראשון לחודיה קדיש איכא למיפרך הא קודם שיצא כולו יצא אחיו וחצץ בינו לבין הרחם וכתיב (במדבר ח׳:ט״ז) פטר כל רחם עד שיפטור כל הרחם. ולר' יוסי ליכא למיפרך דכיון דתרווייהו קדשו כחד דמו:
notes.en: Let us say the Rabbis hold that a portion of the womb: touching the firstborn, sanctifies it. For granted that it is impossible for the births to coincide exactly, and the first alone is sanctified, one can still object: before it came out entirely, its brother came out and interposed between it and the womb, and it is written: “Whatever opens any womb” (Numbers 8:16), [which means] it must open the entire womb. According to Rabbi Yosei there is no objection: since both are consecrated, they are like one.

notes.he: דמתני' דאמרי נותן טלה אחד לכהן דאוקימנא למתני' כרבנן דפליגי עליה דר' יוסי לימא. (ורבנן בין לרבנן ובין ר' יוסי קאמר לימא) קסברי רבנן ואית דאמר ורבנן דפליגי עליה דר' יוסי באידך פירקין כי יצאו ב' ראשים כאחד דאמרי וחכ"א אחד לו ואחד לכהן לימא קסברי רבנן מקצת נגיעת כותלי רחם מקדש דהני כי נפקי ביחד לא נגע בהן רחם אלא לכל אחד מצד אחד:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: of the mishna, who say he gives one lamb to the priest, since we established the mishna in accordance with the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yosei: let us say the Rabbis hold. [A parenthesis in the text: “And the Rabbis,” whether for the Rabbis or for Rabbi Yosei, it says “let us say.”] And some say: “And the Rabbis” who disagree with Rabbi Yosei in the other chapter, when two heads came out as one, who say “one is his and one is the priest’s”: let us say the Rabbis hold that touching part of the walls of the womb sanctifies, since when these come out together the womb touches each of them on one side only.

messages.text: As, if only the entire mouth of the womb sanctifies the firstborn, then in a case where the heads emerged as one, granted that it is impossible for both births to coincide precisely and one certainly emerged first, but in any event there is an interposition, i.e., the head of the other fetus, between each fetus and the mouth of the womb.

notes.he: כלומר מכל צדדין בעינן דליגע בבכור נהי דבאי אפשר לצמצם פליגי דרבנן סברי דחד מפיק רישיה לחוץ טפי מן חבריה:
notes.en: As, if the entire womb sanctifies: that is, we require that it touch the firstborn on all sides. Granted that they disagree about whether it is impossible for births to coincide exactly, since the Rabbis hold that one pushes its head out farther than its fellow,

notes.he: דכל חד וחד חוצץ אחבריה דלא נגע רחם בכל סביביו:
notes.en: There is in any event interposition: since each one interposes for its fellow, so that the womb did not touch all around it.

messages.text: No proof may be drawn from here that a portion of the womb sanctifies a firstborn, as a substance that is in contact with the same type of substance does not interpose. Therefore, each fetus is still considered to be touching the entire womb.
messages.quote: in any event there is an interposition

notes.he: ואלו שניהם מין אחד:
notes.en: A substance with the same type of substance: and these two are of one type.

notes.dh: אמר רב (אשי) מין במינו אינו חוצץ
notes.he: תימה בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין ע.) בעי כרכתו אחותו והוציאתו מהו י"ל הכא מקצת פנוי איכא למימר טפי במינו אינו חוצץ אי נמי אחותו הויא אינו מינו טפי מאחיו עוד יש לומר דוקא משום דהוציאתו שסייעה אחותו בהוצאתו הוא דמספקא לן דדילמא הויא חציצה אבל אם לא סייעה להוציאו פשיטא דלא הויא חציצה וא"ת [לאביי] דמוקי מתני' כר' יוסי הגלילי דאפשר לצמצם ואפ"ה אינו נותן כי אם טלה אחד לכהן משום דכתיב הזכרים אמאי לא אמר כל שאינו בזה אחר זה בבת אחת אינו ולא קדוש לא זה ולא זה וי"ל דלא מסתבר למימר הכי אלא בדבר התלוי במעשה כההוא דקדש שתי אחיות ותודה שנשחטה על שמונים חלות אבל קדושה הבאה מאליה לא אמר הכי ואע"ג דשייך למימר הי מינייהו מייתית הי מינייהו מפקת ואם תאמר מדקאמר נהי דא"א לצמצם חציצה מיהא איכא משמע דה"ק נהי דא"א לצמצם ודין הוא שיקדש האחד לרבנן חציצה מיהא איכא ולא היה לו להיות קדוש משמע דאי הוה אפשר לצמצם היה אז קשה לן היאך קדוש בלא טעם חציצה ומה קשה והא (פריך) [פרישית] דלא אמר כל שאינו [כו'] בבת אחת כו' אלא בדבר התלוי בדבור וי"ל דה"פ נהי דא"א לצמצם ולהכי ניחא לרבנן שאין שתיהן קדושין מטעם הזכרים כמו לרבי יוסי הגלילי דלא אפשר למידרש להו הזכרים כיון דסבירא להו אי אפשר מכל מקום ליהוי חציצה:
notes.en: In brief: [Tosafot read “Rav Ashi said”; the printed Gemara and the English read Rav.] (1) Tosafot ask why, if a substance with its own kind does not interpose, the Gemara in Ḥullin 70a raises a dilemma about a fetus whose sister wrapped around it and brought it out. Three answers: here part of the womb is free, so it is more reasonable to say that its own kind does not interpose; or a sister is less “its own kind” than a brother; or the doubt there arises only because the sister helped bring it out, and had she not, it would plainly not interpose. (2) According to Abaye, who sets the mishna in line with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili (births can coincide) and still gives one lamb because of “the males,” why not apply the rule “whatever cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect at once,” so that neither is consecrated? They answer that the rule applies only to what depends on an act, such as betrothing two sisters at once or a thanks offering slaughtered with eighty loaves, not to sanctity that comes of itself, even though one could ask which of the two is included. (3) The Gemara’s wording “granted that it is impossible to coincide, there is in any event interposition” seems to imply that if coinciding were possible there would be a difficulty without interposition, which the previous answer rules out. They explain the wording: granted that, since coinciding is impossible, the Rabbis cannot use “the males” as Rabbi Yosei does, there should nevertheless be interposition. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: אמר רב אשי מיהא ליכא למשמע דלא בעינן דכוליה רחם מקדש דאע"ג דהכא לא נגע הרחם בכל סביביו דכל אחד כיון דשניהם העוברין מין אחד הן מין במינו אינו חוצץ. וחשיב כאילו נגע הרחם סביב כל אחד:
notes.en: Rav Ashi said [the printed Gemara and the English read Rav]: One cannot infer from here that we do not require the entire womb to sanctify. Even though here the womb did not touch each one all around, since both fetuses are of one kind, a substance with its own kind does not interpose, and it is considered as if the womb touched all around each one.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that if a female donkey that had not yet given birth gives birth to a male and a female, and there is uncertainty with regard to which was born first, the owner designates a lamb in case the male was born first, which he keeps for himself. But since he keeps it for himself, why do I need him to designate it?
messages.quote: he designates one lamb … for himself

notes.he: כיון דלעצמו הוא דלישראל למה לי לאפרושיה:
notes.en: Since it is the Israelite’s own, why do I need him to designate it?

messages.text: It is necessary in order to abrogate its forbidden status.

notes.he: דלפוטרו ממצות עריפה לא היה צריך להפריש מספק כמו שאין נותן לכהן מספק כמו כן אינו עורפו מספק:
notes.en: In order to abrogate its forbidden status: since to exempt it from the mitzva of breaking the neck he would not need to designate a lamb out of uncertainty; just as he does not give [a lamb] to the priest out of uncertainty, so too he does not break its neck out of uncertainty.

notes.he: לאפקועיה לאיסוריה דפטר חמור מיניה שיהא מותר בגיזה ועבודה החמור:
notes.en: To abrogate from it the forbidden status of a firstborn donkey, so that the donkey will be permitted for shearing and labor.

messages.text: Apparently, since prior to the designation the sanctity is not yet abrogated, it is prohibited to derive benefit from the donkey at that stage. If so, whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
It is prohibited to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda; and Rabbi Shimon deems it permitted.
What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda?
Do you have an item that requires redemption and it is nevertheless permitted to derive benefit from it?

notes.he: קודם פדיונו:
notes.en: And it is permitted: before its redemption.

messages.text: And is there no such item? But doesn’t a woman’s firstborn son require redemption with five shekels, and it is nevertheless permitted to derive benefit from him?
messages.quote: Do you have an item that requires redemption and it is nevertheless permitted

notes.he: מותר בהנאה למעשה ידיו קודם פדייה דהא לא אשכחן דאסור:
notes.en: A firstborn son: it is permitted to benefit from his labor before his redemption, since we do not find that it is forbidden.

notes.he: והרי בכור אדם דצריך פדייה ומותר בהנאה מעשה ידיו אפי' קודם שנפדה:
notes.en: But there is a firstborn son, who requires redemption and from whose labor one may benefit even before he is redeemed.

messages.text: Rather, this is what Ulla means: Do you have an item about which the Torah was particular and requires that it be redeemed specifically with a lamb, and yet it is still permitted prior to redemption?

notes.he: וכיון דמחמיר כולי האי שקבע לו הכתוב פדיון בשה ולא באחר ודאי אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: About which the Torah was particular etc.: since [the Torah] is so stringent that the verse fixed its redemption with a lamb and not with anything else, it is certainly forbidden to derive benefit from it.

messages.text: And is the Torah particular about redeeming a firstborn donkey specifically with a lamb? But didn’t Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yosef, redeem a firstborn donkey with boiled vegetables that were worth its full value?
messages.quote: about which the Torah was particular

notes.he: עשבים שלוקות:
notes.en: Beshalkei: with boiled greens.

notes.he: שנותן עשבים שוה דמי החמור לכהן:
notes.en: At its value: he gives the priest greens worth the value of the donkey.

notes.he: בירקות שלוקין נותן לו לכהן מן השלקות בשוויו כמה שוה הבכור ופדאוהו:
notes.en: With shilkei: with boiled greens. He gave the priest some of the boiled greens at its value, however much the firstborn was worth, and redeemed it.

messages.text: Ulla is not saying, i.e., referring to, a case where the donkey is redeemed at its full value. Rather, when we say the Torah is particular that the donkey be redeemed with a lamb, the reference is to redeeming it not at its full value, and this is what Ulla is saying: Do you have an item about which the Torah was particular so as to require abrogating its forbidden status specifically with a lamb, if the lamb is worth less than the donkey? Therefore, Rabbi Yehuda holds that deriving benefit from a firstborn donkey is forbidden.

notes.he: דלא חמיר מהקדשות:
notes.en: We are not speaking of at its value: since it is no more stringent than consecrated property.

notes.he: ואפילו שלא בשויו כדקתני מתני' גדול וקטן:
notes.en: To abrogate its forbidden status with a lamb: even not at its value, as the mishna teaches: “older or younger.”

notes.he: דאם רצה לפדותו בשוויו לא הקפידה התורה עליו דאין יכול לפדותו אלא בשה והכי קאמר יש לך דבר הקפידה התורה עליו לאפקועיה לאיסוריה בשה. כלומר כשאינו רוצה לפדותו בשוויו אין יכול להפקיע איסורו אלא בשה:
notes.en: We are not speaking of at its value: if he wants to redeem it at its value, the Torah was not particular about it [to say] that he can redeem it only with a lamb. And this is what it means: do you have an item about which the Torah was particular to abrogate its forbidden status with a lamb? That is, when he does not want to redeem it at its value, he can abrogate its forbidden status only with a lamb.

messages.text: But this contradicts Rabbi Yehuda’s ruling with regard to second-tithe produce, concerning which the Torah was particular about its being redeemed only with a minted coin, and we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: דאינו מתחלל על אסימון כדכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ה) וצרת הכסף בידך:
notes.en: With a minted coin: since it is not desacralized onto an unminted coin [asimon], as it is written: “And bind up the money in your hand” (Deuteronomy 14:25).

messages.text: If one betrothed a woman with second-tithe produce, if he did so intentionally, he has betrothed her.

notes.he: שנתכוון לחללו:
notes.en: Intentionally: he meant to desacralize it.

notes.he: אם קידש בו את האשה מקודשת. אלמא מותר בהנאה לר' יהודה:
notes.en: He has betrothed: if he betrothed a woman with it, she is betrothed. Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda, it is permitted to derive benefit from it.

notes.dh: ותנן רבי יהודה אומר במזיד קידש
notes.he: משמע הכא דמקודשת בגבולין קודם שיגיע לירושלים והא דאמר בסוף פ' חלק (סנהדרין קיב:) בגבולין דברי הכל פטורין מן החלה לאו משום דחשיב ממון גבוה לכולי עלמא בגבולין אלא משום דלא קרינן ביה עריסותיכם כיון דאסור באכילה וכן עיר הנדחת לאו שללה הוא כדאמר התם בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ צ.) נמי פטר ר"י מחסימה מעשר חוץ לחומה לאו משום דחשיב ממון גבוה חוץ לחומה אלא משום דבעינן דישוי הראוי לו כדממעטינן הקדש ממעילה:
notes.en: And we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says: [If he did so] intentionally, he has betrothed: This implies that she is betrothed outside Jerusalem, before [the tithe] reaches Jerusalem. And what is said at the end of the chapter Ḥelek (Sanhedrin 112b), that outside Jerusalem all agree [dough of second tithe] is exempt from ḥalla, is not because it is considered property of the Most High outside Jerusalem according to all, but because “your dough” does not apply to it, since it is forbidden to eat [there]. Likewise, [property of second tithe in] an idolatrous city is not “its spoils,” as it says there. In the chapter HaSokher et HaPoalim (Bava Metzia 90a) too, Rabbi Yehuda exempts second tithe outside the wall from [the prohibition of] muzzling, not because it is considered property of the Most High outside the wall, but because we require the threshing to be fit for [the animal to eat], as we exclude consecrated property from misuse [me’ila].

messages.text: Apparently, he maintains that deriving benefit from second-tithe produce is not prohibited prior to redemption.

That is not proof, as according to Rabbi Yehuda, if a man betrothed a woman with a firstborn donkey, she is also betrothed. This applies even if deriving benefit from the animal is prohibited, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.

The reason a woman is betrothed with second-tithe produce is that she knows that second-tithe produce is not desacralized by her betrothal. Rather, it remains prohibited, and she will subsequently ascend and consume it in Jerusalem, where consumption of second-tithe produce is permitted. She is therefore betrothed with the benefit of that future consumption.

notes.he: והרי מעשר שהקפידה התורה עליו שאינו יכול לחללו על אסימון אלא על כסף צורה ותנן במס' קדושין ר' יהודה אומר במזיד קידש אם קידש בו במזיד את האשה מתקדשת ומפרש התם מ"ט אלמא דמותר בהנאה (הכא נמי) אמר לך ר' יהודה מקדושי אשה לא מצית מותבת לי דלענין קדושי אשה בפטר חמור נמי מיקדשה כדר' אלעזר דאשה יודעת כו' הכא נמי הא אשה בתר דאיקדשה בפטר חמור פרקה ליה בשה ומיקדשה ליה בהך דביני ביני באותו עודף שהפטר חמור שוה יותר מן השה דהיינו חולין גמורין אבל בהוא עצמו קודם שנפדה אסור בהנאה כדאמינא:
notes.en: But there is tithe, about which the Torah was particular that one cannot desacralize it onto an unminted coin, only onto minted silver; and we learned in tractate Kiddushin: “Rabbi Yehuda says: Intentionally, he has betrothed”: if he intentionally betrothed a woman with it, she is betrothed, and the reason is explained there. Evidently it is permitted for benefit. Rabbi Yehuda could say to you: you cannot challenge me from the betrothal of a woman, since with regard to betrothal she is betrothed with a firstborn donkey too, as Rabbi Elazar [says]: a woman knows etc. Here too, after the woman is betrothed with a firstborn donkey, she redeems it with a lamb and is betrothed to him with the difference between them, the surplus by which the firstborn donkey is worth more than the lamb, which is fully non-sacred. But [the donkey] itself, before it is redeemed, is forbidden for benefit, as I have said.

messages.text: Here too, where one betroths a woman with a firstborn donkey, the betrothal is effective despite the fact that it is prohibited to derive benefit from the animal. This is because a woman knows that a firstborn donkey has a forbidden status and she will therefore redeem it with a lamb. And she is betrothed with that amount, i.e., of the difference between the value of the donkey and the value of the lamb, as the value of the lamb is lower.

notes.he: ששוה החמור יותר מן השה:
notes.en: With that difference: since the donkey is worth more than the lamb.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Shimon, what is the reason he holds it is permitted to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey prior to its redemption?

Do you have an item whereby its redemption, i.e., the item with which it is redeemed, is permitted, but the item itself is forbidden? Here too, since the lamb that is given to the priest is permitted, the donkey that it redeems should have been permitted as well prior to the redemption.

notes.he: כגון הכא שהכהן אוכל את השה בלא שום הקרבה והוא אסור קודם פדיון דהא פסולי המוקדשין שאסורין בהנאה קודם פדיונן הוי פדיונן נתפס בקדושתן ואסור:
notes.en: Whose redemption is permitted: as here, where the priest eats the lamb without any offering, while [the donkey] is forbidden before redemption? For with disqualified consecrated animals, which are forbidden for benefit before their redemption, their redemption takes on their sanctity and is forbidden.

notes.dh: יש לך דבר שפדיונו מותר בהנאה
notes.he: שאין תופסת קדושה בפדיונו שאם פדאו בשה או בדמים יכול כהן למוכרו או נותנו במתנה לכל מי שירצה ואין אסור בהנאה למי שנותנו והוא אסור בהנאה הנפדה:
notes.en: Do you have an item whose redemption is permitted for benefit: since sanctity does not take hold of its redemption, for if he redeemed it with a lamb or with money, the priest can sell it or give it as a gift to whomever he wishes, and it is not forbidden for benefit to the one he gives it to; and the redeemed item is forbidden for benefit?

messages.text: And is there not such a case? But isn’t there the case of selling produce from the Sabbatical Year? As its redemption, i.e., the money received in exchange for the produce, is permitted. But deriving benefit from the produce itself is prohibited after that type of produce is unavailable in the fields, as at that time it must be removed from the house as well.
messages.quote: Do you have an item whereby its redemption is permitted, but the item itself is forbidden

notes.he: המוכר פירות שביעית הדמים מותרין לעולם והפירות עצמן מתבערין בשעת הביעור כשכלה לחיה וקס"ד דהאי מקשה דפדיון שביעית מותר לעולם ולא שמיעא ליה הא דאחרון אחרון נתפס:
notes.en: The Sabbatical Year: one who sells Sabbatical produce: the money is permitted forever, while the produce itself must be removed at the time of removal, when it is gone [from the field] for the wild animals. And the one who raised this objection thought that the redemption of Sabbatical produce is permitted forever, and had not heard that the very last item takes on its status.

messages.text: With regard to the produce of the Sabbatical Year as well, its redemption is forbidden, as the Master says:

If one purchased meat with produce of the Sabbatical Year, both the produce and the meat must be removed during the Sabbatical Year after the point when produce of that kind no longer remains in the field. If one purchased wine in exchange for the meat, the meat’s consecrated status is negated and the wine assumes consecrated status. This process continues until the very last item purchased assumes the consecrated status of the produce of the Sabbatical Year, and the actual produce itself remains consecrated and forbidden following the time of removal.

notes.he: במס' סוכה (דף מ:) לקח בפירות שביעית בשר אלו ואלו מתבערין בשעת הביעור לקח בבשר יין יצא בשר ונכנס יין יין בשמן יצא יין ונכנס שמן ואחרון נתפס בשביעית להתבער ופרי עצמו שגדל בשביעית שבאו אלו מכחו בכ"מ שהוא אסור מן הביעור ואילך:
notes.en: The very last: in tractate Sukkah (40b): if he purchased meat with Sabbatical produce, both must be removed at the time of removal. If he purchased wine with the meat, the meat goes out and the wine comes in; [oil with the wine,] the wine goes out and the oil comes in. And the last takes on Sabbatical status, to be removed. And the produce itself that grew in the Sabbatical Year, from which these came, is forbidden wherever it is, from the time of removal onward.

notes.dh: ולא והרי שביעית דפדיונה מותר בהנאה דאין בו קדושה והיא עצמה אסורה
notes.he: שביעית נמי פדיון אסור דאמר מר אחרון אחרון נתפס בשביעית ופירי עצמו אסור. כדאמר לקח בפירות שביעית בשר ובבשר יין וכו':
notes.en: And is there not? But there is the Sabbatical Year, whose redemption is permitted for benefit, since there is no sanctity in it, while [the produce] itself is forbidden. With the Sabbatical Year too, the redemption is forbidden, as the Master said: the very last takes on Sabbatical status, and the produce itself is forbidden; as it says: if he purchased meat with Sabbatical produce, and wine with the meat, etc.

messages.text: And if you wish, say that Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon disagree with regard to the following verse, as it is taught in a baraita:

With regard to the prohibition against shearing and working a firstborn kosher animal, the Torah states: “You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox” (Deuteronomy 15:19), but you may perform labor with a firstborn animal that is both your own and also that of others, i.e., an animal owned in partnership with a gentile. Although firstborn status applies to the Jew’s share in the animal and he must give the value of his share to a priest, nevertheless, it has no sanctity and deriving benefit from it is permitted.

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

notes.he: עובדי כוכבים כגון בכור בהמה שיש בה שותפות לעובד כוכבים אע"ג דמחייב ר' יהודה למיתב חצי דמיו לכהן שרי בגיזה ועבודה שאין קדושה לחצאין אבל פטר חמור לא ממעט מהאי קרא וכל כמה דלא ממעט לא שרינן ליה דלא גרע מבכור בהמה טהורה ולרבי שמעון ממעט ליה קרא:
notes.en: Yours and that of others: gentiles; for example, a firstborn animal in which a gentile has a partnership. Although Rabbi Yehuda obligates [the owner] to give half its value to the priest, it is permitted for shearing and labor, since there is no sanctity in halves. But a firstborn donkey is not excluded by this verse, and so long as it is not excluded we do not permit it, since it is no less [stringent] than a firstborn kosher animal. According to Rabbi Shimon, the verse excludes it.

messages.text: The verse continues: “Nor shear the firstborn of your flock,” but you may shear a firstborn animal that is yours and that is also that of others. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.dh: אבל אתה עובד בשלך ושל אחרים היכא דיש לעובד כוכבים שותפות בו
notes.he: ואיצטריך קרא צאנך למעוטי להאי דשותפין דעובד כוכבים דשרי בגיזה ועבודה אפי' קודם פדיונן אבל בכורך ממש דאין לאחר שותפין בו אפילו פטר חמור אסור בהנאה ובגיזה ועבודה דברי ר' יהודה ר' שמעון אומר לא תעבוד בבכור שורך אבל אתה עובד בבכור אדם דמעשה ידיו מותר ולא תגוז בכור צאנך אבל אתה גוזז פטר חמור כדאית ליה לר' שמעון דפטר חמור מותר בהני:
notes.en: But you may work with yours and that of others: where a gentile has a partnership in it. “Your flock” was needed to exclude this case of partnership with a gentile, which is permitted for shearing and labor even before redemption. But your own firstborn, in which no one else has a partnership, even a firstborn donkey, is forbidden for benefit and for shearing and labor; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Shimon says: “You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox,” but you may work with a firstborn son, whose labor is permitted; “nor shear the firstborn of your flock,” but you may shear a firstborn donkey, since Rabbi Shimon holds that a firstborn donkey is permitted in these.

messages.text: The verse should be interpreted as follows: “You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox,” but you may do work with a woman’s firstborn son, as no prohibition exists with regard to deriving benefit from the labor of a firstborn boy even before he is redeemed. “Nor shear the firstborn of your flock,” but you may shear a firstborn donkey, as deriving benefit from it is permitted.
Rabbi Yehuda, who does not interpret the verse in this manner, holds that it is prohibited to shear and derive benefit from a firstborn donkey as well.

Granted, according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, that is the reason that two verses, i.e., phrases, are written, one that excludes a woman’s firstborn son from the prohibition against deriving benefit and another that excludes a firstborn donkey.

notes.he: דמוקים לא תעבוד בבכור שורך להתיר עבודה בב"א ובכור צאנך להתיר גוזז בפטר חמור היינו דכתיבי תרי קראי:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Shimon: who establishes “You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox” as permitting work with a firstborn son, and “the firstborn of your flock” as permitting the shearing of a firstborn donkey: that is why two verses are written.

messages.text: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, why do I need two verses to exclude a firstborn animal that is yours and that is also that of others, i.e., owned jointly by a Jew and a gentile, from the prohibition against deriving benefit from the firstborn? And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda, shall we say that deriving benefit from a woman’s firstborn son should also be forbidden, since it was not excluded by any verse?
messages.quote: but you may perform labor with a firstborn animal that is both your own and also that of others

notes.he: ותו לר' יהודה דלא ממעט לעבוד בכור אדם הכי נמי דאסור בהנאה:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, why do I need two verses? And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda, who does not exclude work with a firstborn son, shall we say he too is forbidden for benefit?

messages.text: Rather, everyone agrees that the term “your ox” comes to exclude a woman’s firstborn son, from whom it is permitted to derive benefit. When they disagree, it is with regard to the term “your flock.”

As Rabbi Yehuda conforms to his line of reasoning, as he says that an animal that is owned in partnership with a gentile is obligated in a firstborn, i.e., subject to the requirement that its owner count its offspring as a firstborn, and therefore the verse was necessary to permit shearing and using the animal for labor.

notes.he: וכי איצטריך קרא לר' יהודה למישרא שותפין דעובד כוכבים בגיזה ועבודה לאחר שנתן חצי דמיו לכהן:
notes.en: And where the verse was needed for Rabbi Yehuda is to permit [an animal in] partnership with a gentile for shearing and labor, after he has given half its value to the priest.

messages.text: And Rabbi Shimon holds that an animal owned in partnership with a gentile is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn, and therefore with regard to shearing and labor, no verse was necessary. Rather, the verse was necessary to exclude the case of a firstborn donkey from the prohibition against shearing and working the firstborn animal.

notes.he: ור' שמעון סבר שותפין דעובד כוכבים פטורה לגמרי ולמישרי גיזה ועבודה בשותפות לא איצטריך קרא כי איצטריך לגיזה פטר חמור וה"ה לעבודה דשרי בהנאה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Shimon holds that [an animal in] partnership with a gentile is entirely exempt, and no verse was needed to permit shearing and labor in a partnership. It was needed for shearing a firstborn donkey, and the same is true of labor, since it is permitted for benefit.

messages.text: Granted, according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, this is the reason that the term “your flock” is written, and not simply the word flock. It excludes sheep that are owned in partnership with a gentile. And with regard to the term “your ox,” the word ox alone is sufficient to exclude a woman’s firstborn son from the prohibition; and the verse employed the term “your ox” because of the term “your flock,” so that the two would be stylistically similar.

notes.he: דדריש צאנך ולא של שותפות עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda: who expounds “your flock,” and not one in partnership with a gentile.

notes.he: דמשמע המיוחד לך ולא כתב צאן סתמא. ושורך אע"ג דמצי למיכתב בבכור שור ומימעט נמי בכור אדם מיניה אפי' הכי אטו צאנך כתב שורך:
notes.en: That is why “your flock” is written: which implies that which is exclusively yours; it does not write “flock” without qualification. And “your ox”: even though it could have written “the firstborn of an ox,” and a firstborn son would also be excluded by it, even so it wrote “your ox” because of “your flock.”

notes.he: בשלמא לר' יהודה דמוקים לה למעוטי דשותפין דעובד כוכבים דפטר בגיזה ועבודה היינו דכתיב צאנך כלומר שלך ולא שלך ושל אחרים ואגב דאיצטריך למכתב צאנך ולא צאן כתיב נמי שורך אטו דכתיב צאנך דבשור סגיא למעוטי בכור אדם אלא כתב שורך אטו צאנך:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda: who establishes it as excluding [an animal in] partnership with a gentile, which is exempt [from the restrictions] on shearing and labor: that is why “your flock” is written, that is, yours and not yours and others’. And since it had to write “your flock” rather than “flock,” it also wrote “your ox” because it wrote “your flock”; “ox” would suffice to exclude a firstborn son, but it wrote “your ox” because of “your flock.”

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who derives from the term “your flock” that a firstborn donkey is not included, writing the terms flock and donkey alone would suffice. Why do I need the terms “your ox” and “your flock”? This is difficult.

notes.he: ה"ג היינו דכתיב צאנך ושורך אטו צאנך אלא לר"ש לכתוב שור וצאן:
notes.en: This is the reading: “That is why ‘your flock’ is written, and ‘your ox’ because of ‘your flock.’ But according to Rabbi Shimon, let it write ‘ox’ and ‘flock.’”

notes.he: דלא ממעט שותפות שורך וצאנך למה לי בבכור שור ובבכור צאן סגיא קשיא:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Shimon: who does not exclude a partnership, why do I need “your ox” and “your flock”? “The firstborn of an ox” and “the firstborn of a flock” would suffice. It is difficult.

messages.caption: “Your ox” and “your flock”: what each phrase excludes for Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, in the baraita and in the Gemara’s second reading.

messages.text: The printed text names Rabba here. Rashi reads Rava, the sage who goes on to ask “From where do I say this?”

§ And Rabbi Shimon concedes that even if it is permitted to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey that was not redeemed, following the breaking of its neck in fulfillment of the verse: “And you shall redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck” (Exodus 13:13), it is forbidden to derive benefit from its carcass.

verse.he: וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם־לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: But every firstling donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you must redeem every male first-born among your children.

notes.he: אמר רבא גרסינן:
notes.en: We read: “Rava said.” [The printed text and the English read Rabba.]

notes.he: אם לא פדאו וערפו כדינו:
notes.en: After the breaking of the neck: if he did not redeem it and broke its neck in accordance with its law.

notes.he: להאכילו לכלבו:
notes.en: It is forbidden: [even] to feed it to his dog.

notes.he: שערפו בקופיץ שאסור בהנאה:
notes.en: After the breaking of the neck: that he broke its neck with a cleaver; it is forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: What is the reason for this ruling?
messages.quote: following the breaking of its neck, it is forbidden

messages.text: He derives this halakha by a verbal analogy between the expression: “Breaking the neck,” stated here, and the expression: “Breaking the neck,” stated in the case of the heifer whose neck is broken by the Elders of the city due to a unresolved murder (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9). Just as it is forbidden to derive benefit from the heifer after its neck is broken, so too is it prohibited to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey that was not redeemed following the breaking of its neck.

notes.he: מעגלה ערופה מה עגלה ערופה אסור בהנאה דאתיא שם שם מן ותמת שם דאסורה בהנאה כמת:
notes.en: From the heifer whose neck is broken: just as the heifer whose neck is broken is forbidden for benefit, since “there” and “there” is derived from “and [Miriam] died there,” it is forbidden for benefit like a corpse.

messages.text: From where do I say that this is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon? As it is taught in a baraita (Tosefta, Okatzin 3:12):

The fruit of a tree during the first three years after its planting [orla], and diverse kinds in a vineyard, and the flesh of an ox that was to be stoned for killing or copulating with a person but was slaughtered instead, and that of a heifer whose neck was to be broken but was slaughtered instead,

notes.he: אסורה בהנאה משום דכתיב (דברים כא) שם שם תהא קבורתה:
notes.en: A heifer whose neck is broken: is forbidden for benefit, because of [the verbal analogy of] “there” and “there”: there shall be its burial.

notes.he: ששחטו לאחר שנגמר דינו דלא ירדה בו טומאת נבילות. ועגלה ערופה ששחטה לאחר ירידתה לנחל איתן דקי"ל דהיא אוסרתה:
notes.en: And an ox that was to be stoned: that he slaughtered after its sentence was concluded, so that it did not come to the impurity of a carcass. And a heifer whose neck is broken: that he slaughtered after it had gone down to the stream with a strong current, since we hold that this renders it forbidden.

notes.he: ששחטו לאחר שנגמר דינו דאי נסקל הוה מטמא טומאה חמורה נבלה בכזית:
notes.en: And an ox that was to be stoned: that he slaughtered after its sentence was concluded; had it been stoned, it would impart the severe impurity of a carcass with an olive-bulk.

notes.he: ששחטה לאחר ירידתה לנחל איתן:
notes.en: And a heifer whose neck is broken: that he slaughtered after it went down to the stream with a strong current.

messages.text: and of the birds offered by a leper (see Leviticus 14:4–7), and of a firstborn donkey whose neck was broken, and meat cooked together with milk, are all susceptible to the ritual impurity of food, despite the fact that their consumption is forbidden.

notes.he: אסורין בהנאה במסכת קדושין (דף נז.):
notes.en: The birds of a leper: are forbidden for benefit, in tractate Kiddushin (57a).

notes.he: ששחטו ועדיין מפרכס שלא ירד לטומאת נבילה אבל אם נגע בו שרץ מטמא טומאת אוכלים שאם חזר ונגע באוכלים אחרים מטמאים אע"פ שמפרכס דאמר בהעור והרוטב (חולין קיז:) השוחט בהמה טמאה לעובד כוכבים ומפרכסת מטמאה טומאת אוכלים דמהניא לה שחיטת ישראל למהוי מחשבה הואיל ושחיטה דכוותה חזיא לה בבהמה טהורה. אי נמי אפילו ערפו ממש דנבילה היא ואיכא למימר בהם טומאת אוכלים כגון דאיכא פחות מכזית מינייהו דלא חזי לטומאת נבילות מיצטרף בהדי פחות מכביצה אוכלין ומשלימו לכביצה:
notes.en: And a firstborn donkey: that he slaughtered while it is still convulsing, so it has not come to the impurity of a carcass; but if a creeping animal touched it, it contracts the impurity of food, so that if it then touched other food it renders it impure, even though it is still convulsing. As it says in the chapter HaOr VehaRotev (Ḥullin 117b): one who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a gentile while it is convulsing, it contracts the impurity of food, since a Jew’s slaughter is effective as an intention [to make it food], since slaughter of that kind is fitting for a kosher animal. Alternatively, even if he actually broke its neck, so that it is a carcass, one can speak of food impurity for them, for example where there is less than an olive-bulk of them, which is not enough for the impurity of a carcass, and it combines with less than an egg-bulk of food to complete the egg-bulk.

notes.he: אם נגע בהו טומאה ואע"ג דאינהו גופייהו אסירי מהניא להו להכי שאם נגעו באוכלין אחרים מטמאין אותן:
notes.en: All of them are susceptible to the impurity of food: if impurity touched them. Even though they themselves are forbidden, [their status as food] is effective in this respect: if they touched other food, they render it impure.

notes.he: ופטר חמור כדאמרינן השוחט בהמה טמאה לעובד כוכבים ועדיין היא מפרכסת מטמא טומאת אוכלין משום דמחשבה דשחיטה מכשיר לטמא טומאת אוכלין וכשמתה מטמא טומאה חמורה בכזית כדין נבלת בהמה טמאה שמתה:
notes.en: And a firstborn donkey: as we say, one who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a gentile while it is still convulsing: it is susceptible to the impurity of food, since the intention of slaughter prepares it to contract the impurity of food; and when it dies, it imparts severe impurity with an olive-bulk, like the carcass of a non-kosher animal that died.

notes.he: כדאמרן אע"ג דאיסורי הנאה נינהו:
notes.en: All of them are susceptible to the impurity of food: as we said, even though they are forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: All of them are not susceptible to the ritual impurity of food, since they are all items from which deriving benefit is prohibited and are therefore not considered food.
messages.quote: are all susceptible to the ritual impurity of food

notes.he: הואיל ואסורין בהנאה:
notes.en: All of them are not susceptible: since they are forbidden for benefit.

notes.he: ר' שמעון אומר כולן [אין] מטמאין טומאת אוכלין הואיל דאסור בהנאה ולא היתה להן שעת הכושר (לעגלה) [לערלה] ושור ועגלה וצפרין אמרינן הבהמה בחייה בחזקת איסור עומדת עד שיודע לך במה נשחטה חוץ מבשר בחלב אע"ג דאסור בהנאה מטמא טומאת אוכלין הואיל והיתה לו שעת הכושר קודם שנתערב ונתבשל:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: All of them are not susceptible to the impurity of food, since they are forbidden for benefit and had no period of fitness: for orla [the text corrects “for the heifer” to “for orla”]; and for the ox, the heifer and the birds, we say that an animal in its lifetime stands in a presumption of prohibition until you know with what it was slaughtered. Except for meat in milk: even though it is forbidden for benefit, it is susceptible to the impurity of food, since it had a period of fitness before it was mixed and cooked.

messages.text: And Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to meat cooked together with milk that it is susceptible to the impurity of food, since both the meat and the milk had a period of susceptibility to contracting impurity before they were cooked together.

notes.he: קודם בישול:
notes.en: A period of susceptibility: before cooking.

messages.text: What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Shimon that an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited is not susceptible to the impurity of food? It is as it is written: “All food therein that may be eaten [ha’okhel asher ye’akhel], that on which water comes, shall be impure” (Leviticus 11:34).

verse.he: מִכׇּל־הָאֹכֶל אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל אֲשֶׁר יָבוֹא עָלָיו מַיִם יִטְמָא וְכׇל־מַשְׁקֶה אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁתֶה בְּכׇל־כְּלִי יִטְמָא׃
verse.en: As to any food that may be eaten, it shall become impure if it came in contact with water; as to any liquid that may be drunk, it shall become impure if it was inside any vessel.

messages.text: The use of the Hebrew root alef, khaf, lamed twice in this phrase indicates that specifically food that you are able to feed to others, i.e., gentiles, is called food with regard to susceptibility to the impurity of food. But food that you are not able to feed to others is not called food. Therefore, an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited and which one is consequently forbidden to feed to gentiles is not considered food in this context.

notes.he: לעובדי כוכבים דאינו אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: To others: to gentiles, since [such food] is not forbidden for benefit.

notes.dh: מכל האוכל אשר יאכל אוכל שיכול להאכילו לאחרים קרוי אוכל
notes.he: וא"ת פרק כסוי הדם (חולין פה.) פטרינן עוף טמא מכסוי לרבי שמעון גבי שחיטה שאינה ראויה מדכתיב ציד חיה או עוף אשר יאכל וגו' והא אוכל שאתה יכול להאכיל לאחרים הוא יש לומר התם חיה או עוף כתיב משמע דאתא למעוטי מינים טמאים שאין נאכלין לישראל ואף על גב שיכול להאכילן לאחרים אבל הכא מכל האוכל אשר יאכל משמע שפיר למעוטי שאין נאכל לאחרים:
notes.en: “All food therein that may be eaten”: food that you can feed to others is called food: And if you say: in the chapter Kisui HaDam (Ḥullin 85a), according to Rabbi Shimon we exempt a non-kosher bird from covering [its blood], concerning a slaughter that does not render it fit, since it is written: “Any beast or bird that may be eaten”; but that is food you can feed to others! One may answer: there, “beast or bird” is written, which implies that it comes to exclude non-kosher species, which are not eaten by Jews, even though one can feed them to others. But here, “all food that may be eaten” properly implies excluding what may not be fed to others.

notes.dh: ואמר רב אסי מ"ט דר' שמעון
notes.he: דאמר כולן אין מטמאין טומאת אוכלין דאוכל שאי אתה יכול להאכילו לאחרים הן אפילו לעובדי כוכבים דאסור בהנאה ואינן קרויין אוכל:
notes.en: And Rabbi Asi says: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon, who says all of them are not susceptible to the impurity of food? Since they are food that you cannot feed to others, even to gentiles, because they are forbidden for benefit, they are not called food.

messages.text: Continued on 10a: if so, the Gemara asks, why does Rabbi Shimon need the reason that meat in milk had a period of susceptibility, rather than that it is food you can feed to others?
